open_points.subject: Personal data / read a project context
open_points.text: The customer's contact data reaches the owner alone.
open_points.question: Does `context` (and the project card) give a trusted service with `personal_data` allowed the customer's contact data? R0-26 lets `personal_data` reach such a service, R0-43 hands it `context` with 'customer', and this line says contact data reaches the owner alone.
options: context's 'customer' is only the customer_ref; contact data never leaves to services
services whose token allows personal_data receive contact data too
open_points.default_guess: context carries only customer_ref; contact data reaches the owner alone

open_points.subject: read a project / list projects
open_points.text: owner; a trusted service, in its disclosure class (R0-26)
open_points.question: What does a service whose token does not allow `personal_data` get from 'read a project' and 'list projects', given that the card holds the object's address and R0-26 forbids mixed answers? Is the request refused, or is the service given a projection without personal values?
options: refused unless the token allows personal_data
a separate projection without object/customer
fields above the token's class omitted
open_points.default_guess: refused unless the token allows personal_data; list items carry only id, name and status

open_points.subject: publish / withdraw / read latest artifact for Kernel
open_points.text: read the latest artifact of a type | owner; a service
open_points.question: Are publish, withdraw and read-latest by Cabinet Kernel for the agent confined to the session's project, as R0-41 requires? These rows say 'a service' or 'producer service' without that limit.
options: confined to the session's project like the other Kernel rows
open to Kernel on any project
open_points.default_guess: confined to the session's project; another project is refused

open_points.subject: R0-32 vs R0-42 pinned flows
open_points.text: a later switch or withdrawal changes no flow already running
open_points.question: R0-32 confines agent-authority operations to the project of the current context. How does Registry accept a running flow's calls on its pinned project after a switch or withdrawal, and how does it tell such a call apart from a new one?
options: calls carry the context version they pinned and Registry accepts that version's project
pinning only means the flow keeps the id; Registry refuses its writes after a switch
open_points.default_guess: calls carry the pinned context version; Registry accepts reads and writes on that version's project until the session ends

open_points.subject: agent session
open_points.question: Which action makes an agent session known to Registry, so that the owner can choose a project for it? Who performs that action, Kernel or the owner?
options: Kernel registers or announces a session
the owner names the session
a session exists implicitly from its first Kernel call
open_points.default_guess: Kernel announces a session with its name; the owner then sees it in the owner interface and chooses a project for it

open_points.subject: request a project switch
open_points.text: request a project switch | Cabinet Kernel for one agent session
open_points.question: The agent never sees the catalogue. How does it name the project it asks to switch to? Does the request carry a project_id, or free text the owner resolves? Is a request for an archived project refused?
options: a project_id the owner gave the agent
a free-text description the owner resolves
a request with no target; the owner picks
open_points.default_guess: free-text reason with an optional project_id; the owner picks the project on confirmation, and archived projects are refused

open_points.subject: confirm a switch request
open_points.text: confirming chooses the requested project for that session
open_points.question: What happens when the owner confirms a request whose project was archived after the request was made?
options: refused like choosing an archived project
the request is closed automatically
open_points.default_guess: refused as an archived project; the request stays pending until declined

open_points.subject: Network surface / consumer locations
open_points.text: the service API for services, reachable only on the production host and over the protected channel
open_points.question: Where do Cabinet Kernel, Cabinet and PresuPro run, and how do they reach the service API? The only named channel carries Portal's traffic from the VPS. And how does the owner interface reach the internet over HTTPS from the home server, which publishes no port?
options: all other services run on the home server
the WireGuard tunnel carries every off-host service
an HTTPS reverse proxy fronts the owner interface
open_points.default_guess: Kernel, Cabinet and PresuPro reach the API over the same WireGuard tunnel from the VPS; the owner interface is published through a separate HTTPS reverse proxy

open_points.subject: end of customer relationship
open_points.text: until the relationship with the customer ends, plus one year
open_points.question: Which action records that a customer relationship ended, and who performs it? Is the end derived instead, for example from all of the customer's projects being archived?
options: an owner action 'end relationship'
derived from all the customer's projects being archived
open_points.default_guess: derived from the archiving of the customer's last active project, with no separate action

open_points.subject: R0-37 audit
open_points.text: Every significant operation leaves an audit entry
open_points.question: Which operations are significant? Are services' reads of personal data, agent projection reads and failed or refused requests included?
options: every change plus every personal_data read
changes only
every request
open_points.default_guess: every change, every personal_data read, every confirmation, and every refusal for authorization

open_points.subject: onboard_object role
open_points.text: its role is taken by the owner interface and Kernel flows
open_points.question: onboard_object created projects and customers, but R0-41 says Kernel no longer creates projects. Which part of that role, if any, do Kernel flows take?
options: only the owner interface takes it; Kernel flows only add rooms and pointers
Kernel flows may prepare data the owner then confirms
open_points.default_guess: creation goes to the owner interface; Kernel flows only add rooms and pointers on the session's project

open_points.subject: R0-45 standing
open_points.text: the owner's answers of 2026-10-27 on its conflicts with that frame are recorded as R0-24 to R0-45
open_points.question: R0-45 was 'proposed to the owner ... no objection', not answered by the owner. Is it an owner decision under R0-15, or still open until the owner confirms it?
options: treat no objection as acceptance
mark R0-45 provisional until explicit confirmation
open_points.default_guess: treat it as provisional until the owner explicitly accepts it with the whole
